subtopics.title: From a Single Pulse to a Travelling Wave

questions.question: A pulse is best defined as:
options: A single disturbance that moves through a medium
A repeating disturbance that never stops
The number of waves passing a point each second

questions.question: In a transverse pulse on a rope, the particles of the rope move:
options: Along the rope, in the direction the pulse travels
At right angles (perpendicular) to the direction the pulse travels

questions.question: A ribbon tied to a rope carrying a pulse ends up exactly where it started. This shows that a wave transfers:
options: ENERGY through the medium without transferring matter

questions.question: Two equal pulses, one above the rest line and one below, meet on a rope. According to the principle of superposition:
options: The pulses bounce off each other and reverse
The rope stays flat forever afterwards
They add algebraically — the rope is momentarily flat — and then both pulses continue on unchanged

questions.question: A crest stands 6 cm above the rest line and the trough 6 cm below it. The amplitude is:
options: 6 cm — amplitude is the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position

questions.question: Wavelength is defined as:
options: The height of a crest above a trough
The distance between two successive points IN PHASE, such as crest to next crest
The time for one wave to pass a point
The number of crests per second

questions.question: Two points on a wave are IN PHASE when they:
options: Are both on the rest line
Are one at a crest and one at a trough
Have the same displacement AND are moving in the same direction — separated by a whole number of wavelengths
Have the same amplitude but different wavelengths

questions.question: Points that are OUT of phase are separated by:
options: An odd number of half wavelengths — half a lambda, one and a half, two and a half

subtopics.title: Period, Frequency and the Wave Equation

questions.question: Fifteen complete waves pass a float in 5 s. The frequency is:
options: 3 Hz — fifteen waves divided by five seconds

questions.question: A wave has a frequency of 3 Hz. Its period is:
options: 0,33 s — the period is one divided by the frequency

questions.question: A ripple tank vibrator runs at 20 Hz and produces ripples of wavelength 3 cm. The wave speed is:
Dam waves travel at 1,5 m·s⁻¹ with a period of 0,5 s. The wavelength is:
Before substituting into v = fλ, a wavelength given as 25 mm must be written as:
options: 0,025 m — the formula demands SI units: metres, seconds and hertz

questions.question: A displacement-versus-TIME graph of a wave lets you read off the:
options: PERIOD — because the graph follows one single particle bobbing up and down
Number of waves on the rope

questions.question: You shake a rope twice as fast. What happens to the wave speed and the wavelength?
options: Speed stays the same (it is set by the medium) and the wavelength halves

questions.question: The safest guard against swapping period and frequency is to:
options: Round every answer to two decimals
Write the unit next to every number — an answer in seconds cannot be a frequency

questions.question: In the stadium wave, the spectators move up and down while the wave moves around the ground. This makes it a model of a:
options: Transverse wave — movement at right angles to the direction of travel

questions.question: One ripple of standing-and-sitting running once around the stadium models:
What actually travelled around the stadium?
options: The ENERGY of standing up, passed from seat to seat

subtopics.title: Measuring a Wave with a Skipping Rope

questions.question: On the skipping rope, the amplitude is measured:
options: From the flat rest line up to the top of a hump
From the top of one hump to the bottom of the next
From one hump-top to the next hump-top
From the gate to your hand

questions.question: You shake the rope twice as fast. The humps:
options: Get half as long — twice as many humps fit into the same rope

questions.question: Four whole humps pass your friend's foot every second. Each hump therefore takes:
options: A quarter of a second — frequency and period are the same fact flipped over

questions.question: The time for one whole hump to pass a fixed point is the:
The plain-language reason v = fλ works is:
options: In one second the wave sends out f humps, each λ long — so it advances f × λ metres per second
Speed is always three times the frequency
Wavelength and frequency are always equal
The rope stretches as it moves

questions.question: Twenty ripples a second, each 3 cm long, means the water surface covered per second is:
options: 60 cm — which is 0,6 m·s⁻¹, the same answer as v = fλ

questions.question: A dam wave takes half a second per wave and travels at 1,5 m·s⁻¹. Sharing 1,5 m between the waves that pass each second gives a wavelength of:
options: 0,75 m — two waves per second, so 1,5 ÷ 2

questions.question: The habit that rescues the most marks in wave calculations is:
options: Converting every centimetre to metres and every millisecond to seconds BEFORE multiplying
